name: Push button plan mark
summary: Installation plan mark for a momentary push button, such as a door bell push or call button, shown as a small circle with a dot.
description: On installation plans a momentary push button is drawn as a small circle, often with a smaller concentric circle or dot inside, at the wall position. It is used for door bell pushes, assistance call pushes, door release buttons and timer pushes, with a tag clarifying which.

The symbol is usually linked to the device it operates: a bell or chime, an intercom door release or a timer. Reading the link is important because the same push mark serves very different systems on a mixed plan. It does not show whether the push is illuminated, weatherproof or extra-low voltage. Those are scheduled.
readingNotes: Identify which system the push belongs to from its tag or link.
Check whether it is outdoors and needs a weatherproof rating.
drawingChecklist: Show the link to the operated device.
distinction: A schematic push button shows contacts; the plan mark shows the position of the accessory only.
